title: Crystal growth, magnetic, and transport properties of the candidate altermagnet Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_{2}$
authors: Nashra Pistawala, Martin R. Lees, Geetha Balakrishnan, Daniel A. Mayoh
abstract: Altermagnetism is a rapidly emerging paradigm in condensed matter magnetism, yet the number of experimentally confirmed altermagnetic candidates remains remarkably limited. Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$ has long been theoretically proposed as a promising altermagnet, but there are no reports on experimental investigation of single crystals. Here, we report the successful growth of high-quality single crystals of Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$ and present its structural, thermal, magnetic, and transport properties. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction provides detailed crystallographic information and confirms the hexagonal crystal symmetry ($P6_3/mmc$), one of the criteria for altermagnetic behavior. Resistivity and heat capacity measurements unambiguously identify an antiferromagnetic Néel temperature of $T_N \sim 141$ K. Magnetotransport measurements reveal non-trivial features in the magnetoresistance and Hall response, indicative of quantum diffusive transport phenomena. Cr$_{1/4}$NbS$_2$, synthesized here for the first time in single-crystalline form, therefore serves as an experimental platform for probing the rich spectrum of phenomena predicted for altermagnetic materials.
summary: This work reports the first single-crystal synthesis and comprehensive characterization of $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$, a promising altermagnet candidate. By measuring its structure, magnetic transitions, and transport properties, the authors establish it as a key experimental platform for studying the unique physics predicted for this class of magnetic materials.
main_problem: To experimentally investigate the properties of altermagnets, a class of magnetic materials that challenges the simple ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic classification.
main_result: The authors successfully grew high-quality single crystals of $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$, confirming its hexagonal structure and observing antiferromagnetic ordering ($T_N \sim 141 	ext{ K}$) alongside signatures of quantum diffusive transport.
method: The study employed a combination of techniques, including single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD) for structure, heat capacity and resistivity measurements for magnetic transitions, and magnetotransport measurements for electronic behavior.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Cr}_{1/4}	ext{NbS}_2$, a transition metal-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) proposed as a model altermagnet. Its structure is confirmed to be hexagonal ($P6_3/mmc$), which is crucial for its predicted magnetic behavior.
key_observables: Hexagonal crystal symmetry, Néel temperature ($T_N \sim 141 	ext{ K}$), non-trivial magnetoresistance, and Hall response indicative of quantum diffusive transport.
important_parameters: The stoichiometry $	ext{Cr}_{0.25}	ext{NbS}_2$ and the transition temperature $T_N = 141(1)	ext{ K}$ are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the observed transport anomalies are indeed due to quantum diffusive transport phenomena characteristic of altermagnets.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) shows the grown single crystals, and Figure 1(b) confirms the six-fold symmetry via Laue back-scattering, supporting the structural characterization.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard experimental structure: first, reporting the successful synthesis and structural characterization of the single crystals; second, presenting measurements of bulk properties like heat capacity and magnetic susceptibility to establish magnetic ordering; and finally, detailing magnetotransport measurements to probe electronic behavior.
why_interesting: The investigation into altermagnetism bridges magnetism and electronic transport in layered materials, which is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron behavior in 2D systems.
